name: Kanjanur Agneeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Agneeswarar (Lord of Agni), with the Goddess Karpagambal (Karundhar Kuzhali); the Navagraha shrine for Shukra (Venus)
tradition: Shaiva; Paadal Petra Sthalam sung in the Tevaram; Navagraha Sthalam for Shukra (Venus)
period: Chola period, around the 11th century, with later additions
summary: The Shukra (Venus) sthalam among the Navagraha temples, where Shiva is worshipped as Agneeswarar. Uniquely, Venus has no separate shrine here, for he is held to dwell within the fire of the presiding Lord.

sections.history: Kanjanur stands among the ancient Shaiva shrines of the Kaveri delta, its stone temple built in the Chola period and honoured in the Tevaram hymns as a Paadal Petra Sthalam. Tradition links the place to the lineage of Haradatta Sivachariar and to Brahma's worship of Agni at this spot, and it is counted as the Navagraha temple for Shukra, the planet Venus. What sets Kanjanur apart is that Shukra is given no idol of his own: devotees hold that Venus resides within Agni, the fire, and so within Agneeswarar himself. To worship the presiding Lord is therefore to worship Shukra, a belief that has drawn pilgrims here for centuries as part of the wider Navagraha circuit near Suryanar Koil.
sections.architecture: The temple follows the Dravidian idiom of the Chola country, its sanctum housing the Shivalinga worshipped as Agneeswarar and a separate shrine for the Goddess Karpagambal, known also as Karundhar Kuzhali. In keeping with the temple's central belief, there is no distinct Shukra shrine; the presiding Lord is himself the object of Venus worship. Stone pillars, a modest gopuram and the ordered prakaram enclosures reflect the restrained, well-proportioned building tradition of the region, weathered by age yet carefully maintained. The temple lies close to Suryanar Koil, so that its form and setting echo the shared architectural family of the Navagraha shrines clustered in this part of the delta.
sections.legends: The temple's legends turn on fire. Brahma is said to have worshipped Agni at Kanjanur, and the presiding Lord takes his name, Agneeswarar, from that association with the sacred fire. The tradition of Haradatta Sivachariar, a devotee remembered in the local sthala accounts, is closely tied to the shrine. The most cherished belief concerns Shukra himself: rather than being enshrined as a separate deity, Venus is held to abide within Agni and thus within the presiding Lord, so that the fire that Brahma once honoured becomes the very seat of the planet. Pilgrims accept that worshipping Agneeswarar is a complete worship of Shukra.
sections.festivals: Friday, the day of Shukra, is the temple's most important day, when devotees gather for special worship of Venus. Pradosham is observed through the year with lamp offerings and abhishekam, and the annual Brahmotsavam is the great celebration of the temple calendar. Devotees seeking marital harmony, comfort, wealth and artistic well-being, or relief from Shukra dosha, make offerings of lamps and abhishekam to the presiding Lord, especially on Fridays, trusting that Venus is honoured through Agneeswarar.
sections.experience: Kanjanur is a quiet delta shrine rather than a crowded pilgrimage centre, and it is often visited as one stop on the Navagraha circuit, close to Suryanar Koil. Devotees come chiefly on Fridays to pray to Shukra for marriage, marital harmony, prosperity and artistic gifts, and to seek relief from Shukra dosha. The atmosphere is unhurried and devotional; lamps are lit, abhishekam is offered, and the belief that Venus dwells within the fire of the Lord lends the worship a distinctive quiet intensity. It is a short, meaningful halt for those making the round of the nine planet temples.

visit.timings: Open roughly 7:00 am to 12:30 pm and 4:00 pm to 8:30 pm; timings may vary, so verify locally.
visit.photography: Photography inside the sanctum is generally not permitted.
visit.gettingThere: Kanjanur lies near Suryanar Koil and Aduthurai, about 18 km from Kumbakonam in the Mayiladuthurai/Thanjavur border area of Tamil Nadu. The nearest hub is Kumbakonam; rail access is via Aduthurai or Kumbakonam, and the nearest airport is Tiruchirappalli, about 95 km away.
